metaDescription: Six budget hedge trimmers compared on blade length, branch capacity, corded versus cordless power and 2-in-1 grass shears for small yards and tidy hedges.
introParagraphs: A hedge trimmer is a tool you reach for a few times a season, which makes spending heavily on one hard to justify. The good news is that a modest budget buys a capable machine for boxwoods, privet and small shrubs. The catch is that you have to pick the right power source and blade for the plants you actually own, because a trimmer that is too weak or too awkward turns a one-hour job into a whole afternoon.

This lineup splits cleanly. Two corded BLACK+DECKER models, a 17-inch 3.2 amp and a 16-inch 3.0 amp, rely on a cord and cut branches up to 5/8 inch. Four cordless 2-in-1 tools from Supleap, VERVEWAVE, OGERY and Nicklaua pair a hedge blade with grass shears, and the VERVEWAVE is sold as a bare tool for DEWALT 20V MAX batteries you may already own.

We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback, weighing blade length, branch capacity, battery or cord arrangement, grip and adjustability. We also noted what each model asks of you at this budget, because a tool without a battery or without a clear spec sheet carries hidden work.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 17-Inch Corded 3.2 Amp Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
This is the dependable all-rounder for a typical suburban hedge. The 17-inch blade is the longest in the lineup, so each pass covers more of the hedge face, and the dual-action design moves both blades to reduce vibration and give a cleaner cut. The 3.2 amp motor handles branches up to 5/8 inch thick, which covers normal new growth on boxwood, privet and similar shrubs.

The cost of corded power is the cord itself. You are tied to an outlet or an extension lead, and you have to keep the cable behind you so you do not slice it. There is no battery to charge, however, which also means there is nothing to run flat halfway through a hedge. The listing describes a compact, lightweight body meant to reduce fatigue over longer sessions.

It suits homeowners with hedges within reach of a power outlet. Compared with the 16-inch BEHT100, it offers a longer blade and a slightly stronger motor. Compared with the cordless OGERY and its 8.9 inch blade, it clears far more hedge per pass. Wipe the blades after each use, add a drop of light oil, and keep your cable draped over your shoulder or away from the cutting line.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with an outlet nearby who want the longest blade and no battery fuss.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 16-Inch 3.0 Amp Compact Hedge Trimmer BEHT100
products.description:
The BEHT100 is the smaller sibling, built for compact yards and shrubs rather than long runs of tall hedge. A 3.0 amp motor drives a 16-inch blade that is described as capable of cutting branches up to 5/8 inch, the same capacity quoted for the larger model. The build is compact, which makes it easy to hold for a few minutes of shaping around a doorway or front steps.

Its best feature is the cord retention system. The cord clips in so that a tug on the cable does not unplug the tool mid-cut, a nuisance that wastes time with any corded trimmer. The tradeoff is again the tether and a slightly shorter blade, which means more passes on a long hedge. The listing does not give weight, so judge it by the compact build the maker describes.

It suits renters, small gardens and people who store tools in tight spaces. Compared with the 17-inch model, it covers less per pass but is a touch easier to maneuver. Compared with the Nicklaua and its 9 inch hedge blade, it cuts much more width at once. Store it with the blade guard on, and wipe sap from the blades before it dries.
products.bestFor: Small yards and front-step shrubs where a compact corded trimmer is enough.

Compact build is easy to store and handle

products.name: OGERY 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shears
products.description:
The OGERY is the cordless pick for people who want to trim without a cable and also want a pair of grass shears in the same shed space. It includes two 21V batteries, so you can swap a fresh one in when the first runs out rather than waiting on a charger. The motor is listed at up to 2000 RPM, and the hedge blade measures 8.9 inches.

The short blade means more passes per hedge, but it also makes the tool easy to guide around shaped shrubs and topiary edges. Converting to grass shears turns it into a tool for lawn edges and borders. The compromises are weight, since two batteries and the head add to the tool you hold, and the extra charging to manage for two packs.

This model suits small to medium gardens with a mix of shrubs and lawn edges. Compared with the corded 17-inch BLACK+DECKER, it gives freedom of movement but covers a narrower swath. Compared with the Supleap, it bundles two batteries rather than a display. Charge both batteries after use, and clean the blade of sap with a damp cloth.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want cordless shaping with a spare battery and grass shears.

Converts between hedge and grass heads
Motor listed at up to 2000 RPM
No cord to snag on branches or fences
cons: 8.9 inch blade covers little hedge per pass

Heavier to hold than smaller shear tools

products.name: Supleap 2-in-1 600W 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The Supleap leans on usability. A display on the battery shows how much charge remains, which solves the common cordless frustration of not knowing how long you have left. The blades are double-sided and can be adjusted to several angles, so you can trim the top of a hedge, the side, or tricky corners without twisting your wrist.

Its grip is anti-slip and designed to absorb vibration, and the body is described as lightweight. The 21V, 600W platform is listed as more powerful than the lower-voltage 7.2V tools sometimes sold in this category. What is missing is detail: the listing gives few blade length figures, and wattage is hard to compare with the RPM that other makers quote.

Pick it if you want a user-friendly cordless 2-in-1 for shrubs and grass edges. Compared with the OGERY, it has a battery display but only one battery. Compared with the Nicklaua, it comes with a more powerful stated platform. Charge the battery before storing it, and check the angle lock each time you rotate the head.
products.bestFor: Cordless users who want to see battery level and adjust the blade angle.
pros: Battery display shows remaining charge
Double-sided blades adjust to multiple angles
Anti-slip grip helps absorb vibration
21V platform is stronger than 7.2V models
cons: Few blade length figures to compare
Wattage is hard to compare with RPM

products.badge: Best Bare Tool for DEWALT Owners
products.name: VERVEWAVE Cordless Hedge Trimmer for DEWALT 20V Battery
products.description:
The VERVEWAVE is a niche but sensible choice if you already own DEWALT 20V MAX lithium-ion batteries. It is sold as a bare tool, meaning no battery and no charger, so you save by using what is already in your garage. It combines grass shears and a bush trimmer with two blades that you can swap between, and the listing highlights an upgraded copper-wire motor for power and stability.

The warning is in the listing itself: battery and charger are not included. If you do not own a compatible pack, this is not a bargain, because you will have to buy one. It is also a third-party tool, not made by DEWALT, so there is no manufacturer support from that brand. The listing gives no blade length or weight in the text we reviewed.

It suits DEWALT owners who want an extra attachment for hedges and edges. Compared with the OGERY, which includes batteries, it asks more of you up front. Compared with the Supleap, it uses an existing platform rather than a new battery. Confirm battery fit before you buy and test the lock to be sure the pack seats firmly.
products.bestFor: People who already own DEWALT 20V MAX batteries and want a cheap extra tool.
pros: Uses DEWALT 20V MAX batteries you may own
2-in-1 design swaps blades quickly
Upgraded copper-wire motor for stability
No new proprietary battery to buy
cons: Battery and charger are not included
Third-party tool, not made by DEWALT
Blade length is not stated in the listing

products.name: Nicklaua Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shear 2-in-1
products.description:
The Nicklaua stands out for its rotating head. The head adjusts to three angles, 15, 30 and 45 degrees, which makes it easier to keep the blade flat across a hedge top or a sloping lawn edge without bending your wrist. It includes a 9 inch hedge blade and a 5.3 inch grass blade, both described as made of strong material, and a copper core motor with a no-load speed of 1500 rpm.

Those angles are the main practical advantage, because hedge trimming is largely a matter of wrist position. The tradeoffs are a short blade that needs many passes and a lower stated speed than the OGERY's 2000 RPM. The listing gives no battery capacity or runtime in the text we reviewed, so check the product page for what is included.

It suits small hedges, topiary and lawn edging where posture matters more than speed. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER 17-inch, it cuts far less per pass but needs no cord. Compared with the Supleap, it offers fixed angle stops rather than a battery display. Lock the angle before cutting, and clean the blade after use so sap does not harden.
products.bestFor: Shrub and edge trimming where blade angle matters more than raw reach.

Includes both hedge and grass blades
Copper core motor listed at 1500 rpm

cons: Short blade needs many passes on hedges

buyingCriteria.explanation: This is the first decision, and it shapes everything else. The BLACK+DECKER 17-inch 3.2 amp and 16-inch 3.0 amp are corded, so you never run out of power but you must stay near an outlet. The OGERY, Supleap and Nicklaua are cordless and free you from the cable. If your hedge is farther than a standard extension lead reaches, choose cordless.

Blade length decides how many passes a hedge takes. The BLACK+DECKER 17-inch covers the most, the 16-inch is close, and the cordless blades are 9 inch on the Nicklaua and 8.9 inch on the OGERY. For a hedge over about 10 feet long, favor the longer blades. For topiary and small shrubs, a short blade is easier to control.

Both corded BLACK+DECKER models list a capacity of up to 5/8 inch, which covers new growth but not woody stems. Choose a trimmer for the thickest branch you will realistically meet. For anything thicker than that 5/8 inch figure, use loppers or a pruning saw instead of forcing the trimmer, which can stall the motor.

Cordless tools live and die by their batteries. The OGERY ships with two 21V batteries, the Supleap runs on a 21V pack with a charge display, and the VERVEWAVE uses DEWALT 20V MAX packs that you must supply. If you already own a compatible pack, a bare tool is a bargain. If not, an included battery saves hassle.

Vibration is what tires you out, not weight alone. The BLACK+DECKER 17-inch has a dual-action blade designed to reduce vibration, and the Supleap has an anti-slip, shock-absorbing grip. A comfortable handle matters more when you trim for more than fifteen minutes at a time.

Being able to tilt the head keeps your wrist straight. The Nicklaua offers three set angles at 15, 30 and 45 degrees, and the Supleap has multi-angle blade adjustment. Fixed-head tools like the corded BLACK+DECKER models are fine for flat hedge faces but awkward for tops and corners.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared motor ratings and stated capacities, such as the 3.2 amp and 3.0 amp corded motors cutting to 5/8 inch, and the cordless 21V platforms. Corded models were credited for steady power, cordless for freedom.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade length and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked blade lengths from 17 inch down to 8.9 inch. Longer blades earned credit for large hedges, shorter ones for control around shapes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and cord setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed what comes in the box. The OGERY includes two batteries, the Supleap shows charge on a display, the VERVEWAVE is a bare tool, and the corded models include a cord retention system on the BEHT100.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort and adjustment
howWeEvaluated.description: Grips, vibration control and head angles were weighed. The Supleap's anti-slip grip and the Nicklaua's three angles stood out for comfort, while the 17-inch dual-action blade earned credit for smoothness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at this budget
howWeEvaluated.description: At this level every pick leaves something out. The BLACK+DECKER 17-inch leads on coverage, the OGERY on batteries, the VERVEWAVE on bare-tool savings and the Nicklaua on adjustability. This reflects product specs and buyer feedback.

faq.q: Which is better, a corded or cordless hedge trimmer?
faq.a: Corded models like the BLACK+DECKER 17-inch have longer blades and unlimited run time, but you must stay near an outlet. Cordless models such as the OGERY and Supleap give freedom of movement but have shorter blades and limited battery life. Choose based on how far your hedges are from power.

faq.q: Can these trimmers cut thick branches?
faq.a: Not thick ones. The BLACK+DECKER models list a capacity of up to 5/8 inch, which suits fresh growth. For thicker stems, use loppers or a pruning saw. Forcing a hedge trimmer through woody branches can stall the motor and dull the blades.

faq.q: Does the VERVEWAVE include a battery?
faq.a: No. The listing states that the battery and charger are not included. It works with DEWALT 20V MAX lithium-ion batteries, so it makes sense only if you already own one. Otherwise, a kit like the OGERY with two batteries is simpler.

faq.q: How do I keep the blades sharp and clean?
faq.a: Wipe sap and plant residue after each use, and apply a light machine oil to the blades. Store the trimmer with its blade guard on. Dull blades tear stems rather than cutting them, so replace or sharpen them if the cut looks ragged.

It can be if you also have lawn edges and borders to tidy. The OGERY, Supleap, VERVEWAVE and Nicklaua all swap between hedge and grass blades. The tradeoff is that the hedge blade is usually shorter than on a dedicated corded trimmer.

faq.q: What safety habits should I follow?
faq.a: Wear safety glasses and gloves, keep both hands on the tool, and never trim near people or pets. With corded models, keep the cable behind you. Switch off and wait for the blade to stop before clearing jams, and always follow the maker's instructions.

faq.q: How often should I trim a hedge?
faq.a: Most formal hedges look best with light trimming two or three times during the growing season. Frequent light cuts keep growth thin enough for these small trimmers. Waiting too long leaves thick stems that exceed the 5/8 inch capacity listed for the corded models.
